description: Default architecture, no weight assignment (random init, expected ~0% accuracy).

1-layer, no-LN: attention gathers a,b,c into x=100a+10b+c; MLP computes each output bit as a sawtooth of x via gated [x>=v] comparators (relu(x-v+1)-relu(x-v)), gated by output position; d_ff=1024, hard attention (sharpness 160).
Same 1-layer sawtooth comparator circuit as SawtoothGatedComparators1L, but attention sharpness reduced to 40 (softmax logit ~10 after 1/sqrt(d_head)); tests how soft the gather step can be.
Same 1-layer sawtooth comparator circuit, attention sharpness reduced to 10 (softmax logit ~2.5 after 1/sqrt(d_head)); probes how soft the gather step can be before the digit gather blurs.
Same 1-layer sawtooth comparator circuit, attention sharpness 20 (softmax logit ~5 after 1/sqrt(d_head)); locates the sharpness threshold between 10 (4%) and 40 (100%).

2-layer, no-LN: layer-1 attention gathers x=100a+10b+c; layer-1 MLP builds a shared thermometer code of x ([x>=v] for v=1..255, two ReLUs each) and sums it into 8 sawtooth bit features; layer-2 MLP selects bit j at output position t(j) via relu(bit_j + p_t - 1). d_ff=512.

2-layer, no-LN: attention writes digit-weighted residues c, 2b+c, 4a+2b+c and x=100a+10b+c; bit j is a sawtooth of the residue that determines it (x mod 2^(j+1)), read via shared thermometer comparators (122 units); layer-2 MLP selects bit j by output position. d_ff=128.
Same ResidueThermo2L circuit (needs 122 layer-1 units) with d_ff=64: crashed with IndexError while writing fc1 (only 64 hidden units), before the unit-count assertion.
Same ResidueThermo2L circuit with d_ff set to exactly the 122 layer-1 comparator units needed (no spare hidden units): minimal hidden width for the residue-thermometer design.
Ablation of ResidueThermo2L: layer-2 position gate removed, so BIT = sum of all 8 bit features at every position. Tests whether the position-selection step is necessary.
ResidueThermo2L with attention sharpness 40 (softmax logit ~10 after 1/sqrt(d_head)) instead of 160; checks that the residue design tolerates softer gather attention.
Ablation of ResidueThermo2L without the R2 = 4a+2b+c residue: bit 2 is read from x directly, which needs thresholds at all multiples of 4 on x (d_ff=170).
Ablation keeping only residues c and x: bits 1 and 2 are read from x directly, needing thresholds at all even values of x (d_ff=272). Measures the unit cost of the R1 and R2 residues.
Ablation with no residues: every bit is a sawtooth of x itself (thresholds at all v in 1..255, 510 comparator units, d_ff=512). The baseline that the residue trick improves on.
ResidueThermo2L with attention sharpness 20 (softmax logit ~5 after 1/sqrt(d_head)); tests whether the residue design survives the softer gather that broke the single-layer circuit.
ResidueThermo2L with attention sharpness 10 (softmax logit ~2.5 after 1/sqrt(d_head)); finds where the residue design's accuracy falls off as the gather attention softens.
ResidueThermo2L without the R0 = c residue: bit 0 is read from x directly, needing all 255 thresholds on x (d_ff=552). Measures the unit cost of the R0 residue.

1-layer, no-LN: attention writes residues c, 2b+c, 4a+2b+c, and x; each output bit is a sawtooth of the residue that determines it, built from position-gated comparators in one MLP (174 units). Compares the single-layer and two-layer residue designs.
ResidueGated1L with position-gate strength 256 (the minimum that keeps gated-off units at 0 for x<=255): tests how tight the gate constant can be.
ResidueGated1L with position-gate strength 128, below the 255 needed to keep gated-off units at 0: expected to leak other positions' bit units and fail.
ResidueGated1L with position-gate strength 64, well below the 255 needed to keep gated-off units at 0: checks how badly leakage degrades accuracy when the gate is weak.

ResidueGated1L with the position gate removed (G=0): every bit's comparators fire at every position, so the output is the sum of all bits. Tests whether position gating is needed in the one-layer design.
ResidueGated1L with attention sharpness 20 (softmax logit ~5 after 1/sqrt(d_head)); checks the one-layer residue design's tolerance to softer gather attention.
ResidueGated1L with attention sharpness 10 (softmax logit ~2.5 after 1/sqrt(d_head)); locates where the one-layer residue design's gather attention breaks down.
Compact ResidueGated1L: d_model=36 with 3 heads of width 12 (heads 0,1,2 gather a,b,c), same 174 gated comparators. Fewer parameters than the d_model=64 version, same circuit.
Compact ResidueGated1L (d_model=36, 3 heads) with attention sharpness 20 (softmax logit ~5 after 1/sqrt(d_head)); checks the compact design's tolerance to softer gather attention.
Compact ResidueGated1L (d_model=36, 3 heads) with attention sharpness 10 (softmax logit ~2.5 after 1/sqrt(d_head)); locates where the compact design's gather breaks.
Compact ResidueGated1L (attention sharpness 40) without the R2 residue: bit 2 is read from x directly, needing thresholds at all multiples of 4 on x (d_ff=284).

Compact ResidueGated1L (attention sharpness 40) with only the R0 residue: bits 1 and 2 are read from x directly, needing thresholds at all even values of x (d_ff=512). Measures the cost of dropping R1 and R2.
Compact ResidueGated1L (attention sharpness 40) without the R0 residue: bit 0 is read from x directly, needing all 255 thresholds on x (d_ff=666). Measures the unit cost of the R0 residue.
Compact ResidueGated1L (d_model=36, 3 heads, sharpness 40) with output logit scale L=1 instead of 10; checks that the head only needs the sign of BIT, not a large margin.
Compact ResidueGated1L (d_model=36, 3 heads, sharpness 40) with position-gate strength 1000 instead of 256: a much larger gate constant, checking that nothing depends on the exact gate size.
Compact ResidueGated1L (d_model=36, 3 heads) with attention sharpness 30 (softmax logit ~7.5 after 1/sqrt(d_head)); maps the compact design's sharpness threshold between 20 (74%) and 40 (100%).
Compact ResidueGated1L (d_model=36, 3 heads) with attention sharpness 160 (softmax logit ~40 after 1/sqrt(d_head)): essentially hard attention, the upper end of the sharpness sweep.
Compact ResidueGated1L (d_model=36) with no residues: every bit is a gated sawtooth of x itself (1004 comparator units, d_ff=1004). Measures what the residues save in the one-layer design.
Compact ResidueGated1L (attention sharpness 40) without the R1 residue: bit 1 is read from x directly, needing thresholds at all even values of x (d_ff=402).
Compact ResidueGated1L (d_model=36, 3 heads, sharpness 40) with output logit scale L=0.1: a very weak head; the argmax still only depends on the sign of BIT.
Compact ResidueGated1L with d_ff=173, one unit short of the 174 comparators needed: crashed with IndexError while writing the hidden layer (fc1 has 173 rows).
x-only ResidueGated1L (no residues) with d_ff=1003, one unit short of the 1004 comparators needed: crashed with IndexError while writing the hidden layer.

Final confirmation run: the compact ResidueGated1L design (d_model=36, 3 heads, 174 gated comparators with residues c, 2b+c, 4a+2b+c, sharpness 40, gate 256, logit scale 10) re-run from the saved configuration.
